case_content.title: Prompt #1 - Chilled Beverages
case_content.content: You are consulting for the manager of a division of a large consumer products company. Her division produces fruit juices in three forms, all marketed under the same name: chilled (found in the milk section of the supermarket, usually), juice boxes, and frozen concentrate. This division has sales of $600 million per year. The entire company has sales of over $20 billion. The chilled segment represents $120 million in sales per year. While juice boxes and frozen concentrate are profitable, chilled juices are only breaking even in good quarters and losing money in bad quarters. She has received a proposal from upper management to sell the chilled juices business. What would you advise that she do?

case_content.title: Expected Analysis - Fact Gathering
case_content.content:
To be divulged gradually:

Chilled beverages is a $5 billion dollar industry nationwide. There are two large players that have 40% and 25% of the market, respectively. Your client’s market share, 12%, makes her third in the industry. The best available information indicates that the two market leaders are profitable. The two market leaders are able to fund more advertising and more promotion, trade and couponing that your client. The market leaders produce pure orange juice and blends that are based on citrus juices. Your product uses more elaborate blends of juices, usually with a base of pear or peach juice (95% of the inputs) and flavored with cranberries, bananas, mangoes, etc. (the other 5% of the inputs). Pear and peach juice are about the same price as orange juice, but the other flavorings cost about twice as much. The market for chilled juices is essentially mothers with school age children. This is a highly price sensitive market that loves coupons, promotions, etc. Brand name is important in this market, as in juice boxes and frozen concentrate, as mothers tend to prefer highly reliable products for their children. However, the brand premium must be in line with other branded products. Therefore, all branded juices tend to sell in the same price range. One plant in California produces all of the product, chilled, juice boxes and frozen. It would be difficult to find another use for the plant without a major conversion.

case_content.title: Data / Calculations
case_content.content:
Company and division sales:
- Entire company sales: over $20 billion
- Fruit juice division sales: $600 million per year
- Chilled juice segment sales: $120 million per year

Market size and share:
- Chilled beverages industry nationwide: $5 billion
- Largest player market share: 40%
- Second-largest player market share: 25%
- Client market share: 12%, third in the industry

Input costs:
- Client product base: pear or peach juice, 95% of inputs
- Flavorings: cranberries, bananas, mangoes, etc., 5% of inputs
- Pear and peach juice are about the same price as orange juice
- Other flavorings cost about twice as much

case_content.title: Key Findings
case_content.content:
The chilled juice business is underperforming despite operating in a large market where the leading competitors are profitable. The client is disadvantaged because the market leaders have larger scale, enabling them to spend more on advertising, promotions, trade spending, and coupons. The client’s product also appears to have a higher-cost ingredient mix because it uses more elaborate blends with expensive flavorings, while competitors focus on pure orange juice and citrus-based blends.

The market is highly price sensitive, and branded juices tend to sell in the same price range. This limits the client’s ability to pass higher ingredient costs on to consumers. Brand name remains important, creating synergies across chilled juices, juice boxes, and frozen concentrate. Manufacturing synergies also exist because one California plant produces all three product forms.

case_content.title: Final Recommendation
case_content.content: Based on your analysis, what recommendation would you give the client?

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Final Recommendation
case_content.content:
Solution:

There are three choices:

1. Sell the chilled juice business. This would, however, affect the juice bix and frozen concentrate businesses, as there are both advertising and manufacturing synergies.

2. Sell all of the juice business. This may be more feasible, as the buyer could capture the synergies, but would not be too likely to turn the business around. The selling price is likely to be low.

3. Keep the chilled juice business and rework the ingredients and costs. This turns out to be the most feasible option, as evidenced by the success of the competitors.

A strong candidate should recommend keeping the chilled juice business rather than selling it immediately. The client should rework the ingredient mix and cost structure to make the product more competitive with the profitable market leaders. The recommendation should also recognize the advertising and manufacturing synergies between chilled juices, juice boxes, and frozen concentrate.
